newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH ECON POL ENVIRONMENT SHAKIER OUTSIDE EMU.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH ECON POL ENVIRONMENT SHAKIER OUTSIDE EMU.

text.p: Finnish economic policy must emphasise incomes stability, strong public sector finances and efficient fiscal policy regardless of EMU, but outside EMU the conditions to conduct economic policy will apparently be more unstable, an incomes policy expert group said on Wednesday.

The so called incomes policy committee -- a panel chaired by Martti Hetemaki, head of the finance ministry's economics department, and grouping economists and incomes settlement experts from centrtal trade unions and employer confederations -- said the requirements on economic policy would be similar regardless of whether Finland joined the single currency.
"EMU will lead to increased emphasis on wage formation stability and price stability and on strength in public sector finances and fiscal policy efficiency," the group said in a report.
"Outside EMU, the requirements on economic policy will be the same, but apparently in a less stable environment and at higher costs," it said.

The group said Finnish participation in the third stage of European economic and monetary union would require adjustment to permanently low inflation, but would not cause any particular changes in the national collective bargaining system.

EMU membership would not make it necessary to tamper with current minimum terms of employment, nor with the general coverage of incomes settlement nor would it be necessary to reduce nominal wages, the report said.

On average, the rise in labour costs -- nominal wages, wage drift and employers' indirect labour costs -- should not exceed a percentage equalling the expected rise in productivity plus the targetted rate of inflation, it said.
"In the long run, retaining competitiveness will require that unit labour costs do not rise more than in competitor countries," the report said.

In EMU, public sector wage formation may be steadier than in export branches, where trends may fluctuate more according to sector- and company-specific situations since exchange rates can no longer be used to smooth out cyclical swings.

The use of wage elements based on company performance would increase, the report said, adding it was desirable that the fixed element of wages would develop steadily while result-related elements would fluctuate with business cycles.
The low-inflation goal must be taken into consideration also when deciding on taxes and public charges, the report said.
